shouldFix.title: The specification covers two of the seven retained-evidence members the live G15 row requires, states no retained evidence at all, and gives the offline and upgrade matrix cells no distinct pass condition — yet claims the authoring leftover closes
shouldFix.finding: The live DR-G15 Required-retained-evidence cell enumerates seven members: canonical manifest/tree commitment, provenance/SBOM/license inventory, compatibility/health results, air-gap install, update/rollback, budget measurements, and developer/CI reproduction evidence. The passProperty addresses the first two plus signed-closure fields. The other five are absent from the artifact entirely — 'compatibility', 'health', 'air-gap', 'rollback', 'budget' and 'reproduc' each occur zero times. The matrix names {clean, offline, upgrade} but the same manifest-conformance check is applied in all three, so the offline and upgrade cells carry no distinct pass condition. There is also no retained-evidence statement anywhere: the artifact has no exactByteIntent field and the word evidence does not occur in it.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: Executing the 51 fixtures cannot supply the missing five either. Their classes are TC-NAME, TC-PATH, TC-ACCEPT, TC-DUP, TC-CLOSURE, TC-BYTE-EXACT, TC-SIG and TC-METADATA-ONLY — manifest and schema admission tests. None produces an air-gap install, an update or rollback result, a budget measurement, a compatibility or health result, or developer/CI reproduction evidence. So a harness built to this specification would retain evidence for two of the seven members the register requires, and a later author has nothing to build the offline and upgrade cells from. The artifact nevertheless lists OBL-G15-HARNESS-SPEC under leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded, so accepting it as written would close the authoring leftover on a specification that does not cover the gate.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: Nothing false is asserted: the closure is conditioned on independent ACCEPT, and withholding that is exactly the mechanism working. The corpus has also graded this defect class at this level before — Codex charged core-gate-harness-specifications.v1 with CGHS-V1-SF2 and CGHS-V1-SF3 for naming methods instead of specifying them, both SHOULD-FIX, and I am matching that grade rather than escalating a sibling defect.
shouldFix.repair: For each of the seven evidence members, state what the cell measures, what makes it pass, and what bytes are retained — the per-gate exactByteIntent shape that core-gate-harness-specifications.v3 uses and that this corpus accepted. Give the offline and upgrade cells their own pass conditions rather than repeating the clean-cell check. If some members genuinely belong to a later cycle, say which and why, and narrow the closure claim accordingly rather than claiming OBL-G15-HARNESS-SPEC closes on a two-of-seven specification.

consideredAndDeclined.item: Charging the absence of any DR-120 treatment as a second finding
consideredAndDeclined.observation: schemas.v11's ID-DEP-8 routes 'conformance of adapters to this schema; fixture generation for the test corpus' to 'DR-120 (packaging contract and build-adapter template, OPEN) and DR-G15', with the consequence that v11 defines the contract adapters must emit while 'the adapter template and its ergonomics are DR-120's to design'. DR-120's live row is OPEN, and DR-120 occurs zero times in this artifact.
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: Unlike the DR-125 case at DR-118, where the pinned candidate carried a field literally named dr125ActivationGate saying matrix authoring waits on that closure, ID-DEP-8 does not say the G15 harness specification waits on DR-120. It says the conformance target is v11, which exists, and that only the template's design belongs to DR-120. Charging it would extend an activation-gate finding to a dependency whose source does not state one. I record it so the coordinator can see the adjacency, since a harness that tests adapters will eventually need an adapter template DR-120 has not designed.

consideredAndDeclined.item: Grading the coverage gap a blocker because the artifact claims the closure
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: The closure is conditioned on independent ACCEPT, so rejecting is the mechanism operating as designed rather than a failure to catch a false statement. Codex graded the identical defect class at core-gate v1 as two SHOULD-FIX findings, and matching that is worth more than a harsher grade on a sibling.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Fourteen attacks run, one landed. Custody holds: subject 384c3d8a at 0444 unmoved with dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left 5d5d778, file 08 at 3a9442d1 equal to the subject's own pin, governing tree clean, and all four cited digests reproduce. Much of this is right. claimVerbatim is byte-exact against the live claim cell, the gate owner is byte-exact and kept distinct from DR-103's row owner so the DR-101 collapse defect is not repeated, the identifier occurs in its own live harness cell, and the matrix shape matches the live adapter × platform × clean/offline/upgrade wording with the adapter axis correctly narrowed to slice-1 TypeScript. The 51 fixtures are held unexecuted, the three unauthored classes are held unauthored with unicode-norm correctly blocked on a later schema successor, OD-1 and OD-2 are refused five times each, Rust-as-core is refused, and the five remaining leftover obligations are exactly D-161's six minus this one. The objection is coverage. The live G15 Required-retained-evidence cell enumerates seven members and the passProperty addresses two of them plus signed-closure fields; compatibility, health, air-gap, rollback, budget and reproduc each occur zero times in the artifact. There is no retained-evidence statement at all — no exactByteIntent field, and the word evidence does not appear. The matrix names clean, offline and upgrade but applies the same manifest-conformance check in all three, so two of the three states have no distinct pass condition. Executing the 51 fixtures cannot fill the gap either: their classes are TC-NAME, TC-PATH, TC-ACCEPT, TC-DUP, TC-CLOSURE, TC-BYTE-EXACT, TC-SIG and TC-METADATA-ONLY, all manifest and schema admission tests, none of which yields an air-gap install, an update or rollback result, a budget measurement, a compatibility or health result, or CI reproduction evidence. The artifact nonetheless lists OBL-G15-HARNESS-SPEC under the closure field, so accepting it as written would close the authoring leftover on a specification covering two of seven. I graded it SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker because the closure is conditioned on independent ACCEPT — withholding that is the mechanism working — and because Codex graded the identical defect class at core-gate v1 as two SHOULD-FIX findings. One item is recorded as considered and declined: schemas.v11's ID-DEP-8 routes the adapter template to DR-120, which is OPEN and which this artifact never mentions. I did not charge it, because unlike the DR-125 gate at DR-118 the source does not say the harness specification waits on that closure — but a harness that tests adapters will eventually need a template DR-120 has not designed, and you may want that adjacency on the record.
